content:
maya: Heads-up — I'm seeing the Python SDK async client drop the x-request-id / trace propagation when using OpenTelemetry instrumentation. Minimal repro below, happens reliably in our staging runs.

maya: ```py
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from opentelemetry import trace
from opentelemetry.propagate import inject

tracer = trace.get_tracer(__name__)

async def call():
    async with RedwoodClient(api_key="$REDWOOD") as client:
        with tracer.start_as_current_span("test"):
            # expecting x-request-id / traceparent on outbound request
            await client.generate("Hello")
```

maya: Logs show no trace headers on the outgoing HTTP request (aiohttp transport):
maya: `OUTBOUND HTTP: headers={} // missing traceparent/x-request-id`

sam: Is this only with async context manager? sync client OK? Which SDK version?

maya: async only so far, testing with python-sdk 0.9.3rc1 (nightly build). Sync client appears to propagate correctly.

sam: Can you paste a minimal repro that I can run locally (requirements + exact snippet)? Also which OTEL propagator stack are you using (tracecontext/b3)?

maya: Using W3C TraceContext (default). Quick repro attached to the issue I just filed: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/517 — includes small aiohttp server to inspect headers.

ana: tagging @ana — I think this matches the middleware ordering bug we saw last month where the retry/middleware chain ran after instrumentation for async paths. The sync path used a different callflow.

ana: (typo) sorry, meant @ana

ana: (reposting) @ana — see above

ana -> ana: (no direct message shown)

ana: (ignore previous two lines, threading hiccup)

ana: @maya thanks for the issue. I dug in and it looks like the async transport creates a fresh aiohttp.ClientSession per call and the instrumentation wrapper is applied at a different layer than for sync. There's a draft PR that aims to unify the middleware order: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/489 (WIP).

lee: Workaround until PR lands: manually instrument the session and pass a session into the client constructor so the traced session is used for all requests. Example:
lee: ```py
from opentelemetry.instrumentation.aiohttp_client import create_trace_config
import aiohttp

trace_config = create_trace_config()
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(trace_configs=[trace_config])
client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., _session=session)  # internal usage for workaround
```
lee: Not ideal but works in a pinch.

isaac: Typing note: the AsyncRedwoodClient.__aenter__ signature currently returns Any in our stubs which hides some mypy issues — we should return "AsyncRedwoodClient" explicitly. Filed https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/issues/503 for the typing fix.

deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Staging deploy: sdk-e2e-tests failed — tests/otel/test_request_id_propagation.py::test_async_missing_headers — job 8421 — https://ci.redwood-inference/internal/8421/logs

maya: I pushed a small PR with a failing test captured and a proposed fix that ensures the opentelemetry propagator is applied to the aiohttp session used by the async client. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/python-sdk/pull/522

sam: Nice, can you also add an integration test that exercises both sync and async clients with the same OTEL config? Add a note to devex/observability.md about the workaround and the planned fix.

ana: @sam +1. Also add a short release-note blurb and mark it as a potential breaking change for users who relied on internal _session behavior (we should call out the workaround).

ana: I'll review PR #522 tomorrow morning. If green, we should backport to 0.9.x since it's a regression for observability.

maya: Thanks — in the PR I've also added an explicit header pass-through layer to ensure x-request-id isn't dropped by retry/redirect handling. Test reproduces redirect + retry + propagation.

lee: After the fix lands we should add a small sample app to the examples/observability folder showing OTEL + request-id + async usage. That'll help onboarding.

isaac: Also update typeshed stubs so IDEs show correct async context manager return type. I'll open a follow-up PR for type-only changes.

sam: Sounds good. tagging everyone: @maya @ana @lee @isaac — thanks for catching this, very visible for customers using tracing.

maya: Please ping me if CI keeps flaking. I'll iterate on the test if needed. :thumbsup:
